worked_example.problem: Mother gives Ashu {money} FCFA for the market. The family needs rice, palm oil, salt and soap. Ashu would also like sweets. Plan the list.
steps: Needs first: rice {rice} FCFA, palm oil {oil} FCFA, salt {salt} FCFA, soap {soap} FCFA.
Add the needs: {rice} + {oil} + {salt} + {soap} = {rice + oil + salt + soap} FCFA.
Money left: {money} − {rice + oil + salt + soap} = {money - rice - oil - salt - soap} FCFA.
The sweets cost {sweets} FCFA, which is not more than what is left, so they can go last on the list.
worked_example.answer: Rice, palm oil, salt, soap, then sweets. Total: {rice + oil + salt + soap + sweets} FCFA.
checks: rice + oil + salt + soap + sweets <= money

cards.idea: Needs are things we must have. Wants are nice to have, but we can live without them.
example: Wants: sweets, a toy car, soft drinks.

check.prompt: Sort each item: is it a need or a want?

cards.idea: Buy the needs first. Add up the prices: the total must not be more than the money you have.
example: You have {money} FCFA. Rice costs {a} FCFA and soap costs {b} FCFA.
{a} + {b} = {a + b} FCFA, so {money - a - b} FCFA is left.

cards.idea: Write one item on each line, with the quantity and the price. Put a title at the top and the total at the bottom.

check.prompt: Which line is written the right way for a shopping list?

wrong.explain: Give the quantity and the price too.

wrong.text: I will buy some salt because we need it for the soup.
wrong.explain: A list has short lines, not full sentences.

wrong.text: Salt and soap and rice and oil
wrong.explain: Write one item on each line.

paper_task.prompt: Your family has {money} FCFA for the market on Saturday. Write a shopping list for the week in your exercise book. Put the needs first, give the quantity and the price of each item, and add up the total.
model: Sweets for my little brother — {sweets} FCFA
Total: {rice + oil + beans + salt + soap + books + sweets} FCFA (money left: {money - rice - oil - beans - salt - soap - books - sweets} FCFA)
checklist: Each item is on its own line.
Each item has a quantity and a price.
The needs come before the wants.
I added up the prices and wrote the total.
My total is not more than {money} FCFA.
checks: rice + oil + beans + salt + soap + books + sweets <= money
